The LAO has deposited a sum of Rs.14,40,000/- and the said amount has been kept in F.D., in the Karnataka Bank Limited, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to the claimants and Objectors.
The claimants and Objectors have appeared through their counsels and filed separate claim statements.

.5. Claimants 1 to 3 filed claim statement claiming that they are the sole and absolute owners of the immovable property bearing Survey No. 21/3 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk.
The claimant No.1 A.N. Subbappa purchased the said property under a registered sale deed dated 05.09.1980.
Accordingly the property has been changed to the name of claimant No.1.

The said property has been acquired by the -5- : L.A.C. No.97/2005:
respondent.
Accordingly claims that they are entitled for compensation in respect of acquired property.

.6. The Objectors 1 to 3 filed common claim statement claiming that the acquired property in Survey No.21/3 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R.
Puram Hobli originally belongs to the claimants and they have agreed to sell the acquired property in favour of objector No.1 for a total sale consideration of Rs.7,20,000/- and executed a sale agreement dated 13.03.1995 by receiving part sale consideration of Rs. 6,50,000/-.
Thereafter, the said land has been acquired by the respondent.
It is further stated that in view of acquisition of property, the Objectors are unable seek the specific performance of contract.

Further it is stated that they have filed writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.
No.35958-979/2002 and connected W.P. No.26272/2001 and 28689/2001.

Further they have also filed an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act seeking reference to the Court for -6- : L.A.C. No.97/2005:
enhancement of compensation.
Accordingly claim that they are entitled for compensation amount involved in this case.
.7. The claimants though filed claim statement not led any oral evidence nor produced any documentary evidence.

.8. The Objector No.1(c) K.V. Sathyanarayana is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7.
.9.

On the basis of the above, the points for consideration are that:
1) Whether the claimants 1 to 3 are entitled to receive the compensation to an extent of 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka Subbappa A N vs Spl Lao Kiadb on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131380444/
3 as claimed in their claim statement?
2) Whether the Objectors 1 to 3 are entitled to receive the compensation to an extent of 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka as claimed in their claim statement?
3) What Order or Award?

REASONS .11. Points 1 and 2: It is an admitted fact that the land bearing Sy.No.21/3 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka has been acquired under Preliminary notification dated 24.11.1998 and final notification dated 27.06.2002 and the award has been passed on 09.06.2004.
It is an admitted fact that the L.A.O., has awarded a sum of Rs.14,40,000/- and the said amount has been kept in F.D., in the Karnataka Bank Limited, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru.

It is undisputed fact that the property originally belongs to the claimant -8- : L.A.C. No.97/2005:

.12.

In this case, there is no dispute between parties that the property in Survey No.
21/3 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas of Kundalahalli village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka belongs to the claimant No.1 A.N. Subbappa as he has purchased the said property under a registered sale deed dated 05.09.1980.
The claimants 2 and 3 are the children of claimant No.1 A.N. Subbappa.

.13. The case made out by the Objectors in their objection statement is that claimants 1 to 3 agreeing to sell the said property in their favour and executed a registered sale agreement dated 13.03.1995 after receipt of part sale consideration of Rs.6,50,000/- and balance sale consideration was only Rs.70,000/- and that has to be paid at the time of registration.
Therefore, the claim of the Objectors in this case is based on the sale agreement.

Therefore, the Objectors have to prove that the claimants have executed a sale agreement, agreeing -9- : L.A.C. No.97/2005:

sentences.text: In this case, though the claimants filed their claim statement as on 19.12.2008 not chosen to lead oral and documentary evidence.
Apart from that they have also not chosen to cross examine the PW.1 who had been examined on behalf of the Objectors.

As stated earlier, the undisputed fact is that the property originally belongs to the claimant No.1 who has purchased the said property under a registered sale deed.
.15.

The specific claim of the Objectors in this case is that the claimants 1 to 3 agreed to sell the said property in their favour and after receiving the substantial part sale consideration amount of Rs.6,50,000/- executed a registered sale agreement and the balance sale consideration amount was only Rs.70,000/-.

In support of the said contention, the Objectors have produced registered sale agreement at - 10 : L.A.C. No.97/2005:
-
Ex.P.1, which reveals that claimants 1 to 3 executed a registered sale agreement in respect of acquired property by receiving part sale consideration of Rs.6,50,000/-
and balance sale consideration was only Rs. 70,000/-.
It is also not in dispute that the property had been acquired by the B.D.A., as such, it is not possible for the Objectors to enforce the sale agreement entered between them with claimants.
Further execution of sale agreement is not disputed by the claimants in their claim statement.

It is also relevant to note that even prior to the filing of claim statement,
there was a dispute between parties before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Writ Petition and also these Objectors filed an application before the LAO claiming right over the acquired property.
Inspite of that the claimants in their claim statement not stated anything about the execution of sale agreement nor disputed the execution of sale agreement.

Under such circumstances, the only inference that could be drawn that the claimants 1 to 3 have executed a registered sale agreement at Ex.P.1 by - 11 : L.A.C. No.97/2005:
-
receiving substantial sale consideration of Rs.6,50,000/-.
.16.

In the case on hand, the material on record clearly reveals that the original owners of the land / claimants 1 to 3 executed a registered sale agreement in favour of Objectors agreeing to sell the property.

sentences.text: Now the point to be considered is that whether agreement holder is entitled to receive the compensation amount.

In this context it is useful to refer the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case of Sukhbir Vs. Ajit Singh reported in (2021) 6 SCC 54, wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that:
"the Buyer under the contract for sale would be deemed to have stepped into shoes of owner-vendor and thus, such buyer is entitled to entire amount of compensation along with solatium and interest etc., as payable to the owner under Land Acquisition Act."

entities.text: Sukhbir Vs. Ajit Singh reported in (2021) 6 SCC 54
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, certainly these objectors are entitled to receive the compensation.

However, the liberty has to - 12 : L.A.C. No.97/2005:
-
be given to the claimants to receive the balance sale consideration amount out of compensation amount with the applicable interest in compensation.

Therefore, as per the Principle laid down by the Apex Court in a case of Sukhbir Vs. Ajit Singh, the Objectors are entitled for compensation for 1 acre 8 guntas of land subject to payment of balance sale consideration amount of Rs. 70,000/- to the claimants with accrued interest.
Accordingly, the above points 1 and 2 are answered partly in the affirmative.
.18. Point No.3:
In view of my findings on the above points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

ORDER The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is hereby partly allowed.

Objectors are entitled for compensation for 1 acre 8 guntas of land excluding balance sale consideration amount of Rs. 70,000/- that has to be paid to the claimants with accrued interest on the said amount.

which amount they are going to receive in this case.
Draw award accordingly.
